definitions.gloss: shopping bag
definitions.explanation: A bag used to carry purchased goods, whether a reusable bag brought from home or a bag provided at a store.

examples.japanese: {買|か}い{物袋|ものぶくろ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っていく→持っていく：27431_motteiku⟧。
examples.english: I'll bring a shopping bag.

examples.japanese: {買|か}い{物袋|ものぶくろ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{重|おも}くて→重い：00804_omoi⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痛|いた}い→痛い：01108_itai⟧。
examples.english: The shopping bag is so heavy my hands hurt.

examples.japanese: ⟦レジ{袋|ぶくろ}→レジ袋：09531_rejibukuro⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{有料|ゆうりょう}→有料：03178_yuuryou⟧になった⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、{買|か}い{物袋|ものぶくろ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れない→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧ようにして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。

Compound of ⟦{買|か}い{物|もの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧ (shopping) and {袋|ぶくろ} (bag). Since Japan made plastic bags (⟦レジ{袋|ぶくろ}→レジ袋：09531_rejibukuro⟧) paid at stores in 2020, the word {買|か}い{物袋|ものぶくろ} is now commonly associated with reusable bags (⟦エコバッグ→エコバッグ：08937_ekobaggu⟧) that shoppers bring themselves.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {買|か}い{物袋|ものぶくろ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持参|じさん}する→持参する：21143_jisansuru⟧: to bring one's own shopping bag
- {買|か}い{物袋|ものぶくろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧: to put in a shopping bag
- {買|か}い{物袋|ものぶくろ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れる→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧: to forget one's shopping bag

RELATED WORDS:

- ⟦エコバッグ→エコバッグ：08937_ekobaggu⟧: reusable bag; eco bag — a loanword commonly used for reusable shopping bags
- ⟦{紙袋|かみぶくろ}→紙袋：09705_kamibukuro⟧: paper bag

entry.gloss: to turn one's attention to; to look toward

definitions.gloss: to look toward; to turn one's eyes to
definitions.explanation: To physically direct one's gaze toward something.

definitions.gloss: to turn one's attention to; to pay attention to; to focus on
definitions.explanation: To direct one's awareness or interest toward an issue, topic, or aspect. The figurative meaning is more common.

examples.english: I turned my eyes toward the window.
He looked in this direction.
When I looked toward the voice, my friend was standing there.

examples.japanese: ⟦{環境|かんきょう}{問題|もんだい}→環境問題：10136_kankyoumondai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{目|め}を{向|む}ける。
examples.english: To turn one's attention to environmental issues.

examples.japanese: ⟦{海外|かいがい}→海外：00134_kaigai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{目|め}を{向|む}ける⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: We need to turn our attention overseas as well.

examples.japanese: ⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{原因|げんいん}→原因：01400_genin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦もっと→もっと：00798_motto⟧{目|め}を{向|む}けるべきだ。
examples.english: We should pay more attention to the cause of the problem.

entry.notes:
Literally 'to direct one's eyes toward.' The figurative sense (paying attention to an issue or topic) is more common in written and formal Japanese. The expression emphasizes a deliberate, conscious act of focusing attention.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{現実|げんじつ}→現実：02720_genjitsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{目|め}を{向|む}ける: to face reality
- ⟦{未来|みらい}→未来：03748_mirai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{目|め}を{向|む}ける: to look toward the future
- ⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{目|め}を{向|む}ける: to turn attention to a problem
- ⟦{世界|せかい}→世界：01447_sekai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{目|め}を{向|む}ける: to look out at the world

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{注目|ちゅうもく}する→注目する：25530_chuumokusuru⟧: to pay attention to — more about focusing closely on something noteworthy
- {目|め}を{向|む}ける is about deliberately directing attention, often toward something previously overlooked
- ⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧そらす: to look away; to avert one's eyes — the opposite action

entry.gloss: just after a bath; fresh from the bath

definitions.gloss: just after a bath; fresh from the bath
definitions.explanation: The state or moment immediately after getting out of a bath or hot spring. Also used as a modifier for things used or done right after bathing.

examples.japanese: {湯上|ゆあ}がり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ビール→ビール：01015_biiru⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{最高|さいこう}→最高：02637_saikou⟧だ。
examples.english: A beer right after a bath is the best.

examples.japanese: {湯上|ゆあ}がり⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{冷|つめ}たい→冷たい：00681_tsumetai⟧⟦{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}→牛乳：00777_gyuunyuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}んだ→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。
examples.english: I drank cold milk right after the bath.

examples.japanese: {湯上|ゆあ}がり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{肌|はだ}→肌：02243_hada⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{乾燥|かんそう}→乾燥：00184_kansou⟧しやすい⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦すぐ→すぐ：00814_sugu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{保湿|ほしつ}→保湿：11617_hoshitsu⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{方|ほう}→方：01139_hou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: Skin right after a bath dries out easily, so it's best to moisturize right away.

examples.japanese: ⟦{温泉|おんせん}→温泉：04117_onsen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{湯上|ゆあ}がり⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{浴衣|ゆかた}→浴衣：04081_yukata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}て→着る：00541_kiru⟧⟦{旅館|りょかん}→旅館：01049_ryokan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{廊下|ろうか}→廊下：05005_rouka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{気持|きも}ち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: It feels wonderful to walk through the ryokan hallway in a yukata after the hot spring.

entry.notes:
Compound of ⟦{湯|ゆ}→湯：01740_yu⟧ (hot water/bath) and ⟦{上|あ}がり→上がる：00615_agaru⟧ (coming out of). Strongly associated with Japanese bathing culture — especially ⟦{温泉|おんせん}→温泉：04117_onsen⟧ (hot springs) and ⟦{銭湯|せんとう}→銭湯：16032_sentou⟧ (public baths). The image of drinking cold milk or beer after a bath is a classic cultural reference.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {湯上|ゆあ}がり⟦タオル→タオル：01533_taoru⟧: bath towel (for after bathing)
- {湯上|ゆあ}がり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{肌|はだ}→肌：02243_hada⟧: skin fresh from the bath
- {湯上|ゆあ}がり⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧: to drink right after bathing
- {湯上|ゆあ}がり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一杯|いっぱい}→一杯：01793_ippai⟧: a drink right after the bath

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{風呂上|ふろあ}がり→風呂上がり：22451_furoagari⟧: after a bath — essentially synonymous, but ⟦{風呂上|ふろあ}がり→風呂上がり：22451_furoagari⟧ is slightly more colloquial
- {入浴後|にゅうよくご}: after bathing — more formal and clinical

CULTURAL NOTE:
Drinking cold ⟦{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}→牛乳：00777_gyuunyuu⟧ (milk) in the changing room of a ⟦{銭湯|せんとう}→銭湯：16032_sentou⟧ after bathing is a beloved Japanese custom, often depicted in media.

sol_flags.concern: 冬眠 can be used figuratively for prolonged inactivity, including a company's inactivity; the categorical exclusion is incorrect.

definitions.gloss: dormancy; hibernation; lying inactive
definitions.explanation: A state of inactivity in biological organisms (plants, animals, seeds) during unfavorable conditions.

definitions.gloss: lying dormant; being inactive
definitions.explanation: Used figuratively for accounts, companies, or organizations that exist but are not currently active.

examples.english: During winter, the seeds go dormant.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{植物|しょくぶつ}→植物：03248_shokubutsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{休眠|きゅうみん}⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧。

examples.english: Let the bulb go dormant in a cool place before planting it.

examples.japanese: {休眠口座|きゅうみんこうざ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please be aware of dormant accounts.

examples.japanese: {休眠|きゅうみん}⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{届|とど}け{出|で}た→届け出る：05910_todokederu⟧。
examples.english: It was registered as a dormant company.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧{休眠|きゅうみん}⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{特許|とっきょ}→特許：13467_tokkyo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{再|ふたた}び→再び：03600_futatabi⟧⟦{注目|ちゅうもく}→注目：03483_chuumoku⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A patent that had been lying dormant for years is attracting attention again.

entry.notes:
Compound of {休|きゅう} (rest) and {眠|みん} (sleep). Originally a biological term for the inactive period of organisms, now widely used in business and finance for inactive entities.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {休眠|きゅうみん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to go dormant
- {休眠|きゅうみん}⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧: dormant state
- {休眠口座|きゅうみんこうざ}: dormant account
- {休眠|きゅうみん}⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧: dormant company
- {休眠|きゅうみん}⟦{期間|きかん}→期間：00229_kikan⟧: dormancy period

definitions.gloss: republic; republican system of government
definitions.explanation: A system of government in which the head of state is elected or appointed rather than inheriting the position, and sovereignty rests with the people.

examples.japanese: ⟦フランス→フランス：19418_furansu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{共和制|きょうわせい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧だ。
examples.english: France is a republic.

examples.japanese: ⟦{革命|かくめい}→革命：05968_kakumei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧、{共和制|きょうわせい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{樹立|じゅりつ}→樹立：13232_juritsu⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: After the revolution, a republic was established.

examples.japanese: ⟦{君主制|くんしゅせい}→君主制：21776_kunshusei⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{共和制|きょうわせい}⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{移行|いこう}→移行：13776_ikou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{平和的|へいわてき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|おこな}われた→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: The transition from monarchy to republic was carried out peacefully.

entry.notes:
Compound of ⟦{共和|きょうわ}→共和：18656_kyouwa⟧ (republic/republican) and ⟦{制|せい}→〜制：30791_sei⟧ (system). The ⟦{制|せい}→〜制：30791_sei⟧ suffix indicates a system of governance, as in ⟦{君主制|くんしゅせい}→君主制：21776_kunshusei⟧ (monarchy) or {民主制|みんしゅせい} (democracy).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {共和制|きょうわせい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{樹立|じゅりつ}→樹立：13232_juritsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to establish a republic
- {共和制|きょうわせい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧: a republican nation
- {共和制|きょうわせい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{移行|いこう}→移行：13776_ikou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to transition to a republic
- ⟦{大統領|だいとうりょう}→大統領：03418_daitouryou⟧{共和制|きょうわせい}: presidential republic

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{共和国|きょうわこく}→共和国：24322_kyouwakoku⟧: republic (as a country) — refers to a specific republican nation, while {共和制|きょうわせい} refers to the system itself
- ⟦{君主制|くんしゅせい}→君主制：21776_kunshusei⟧: monarchy — government headed by a hereditary ruler, the opposite system
- {民主制|みんしゅせい}: democracy — government by the people, can coexist with {共和制|きょうわせい}
- {立憲制|りっけんせい}: constitutional government — government based on a constitution

sol_flags.concern: Junmai can combine with ginjo and daiginjo, but not honjozo: honjozo requires added brewing alcohol, whereas junmai excludes it.
sol_flags.suggestion: Change the parenthetical to “can be combined with ginjo or daiginjo.”

sol_flags.concern: In standard sake terminology, 冷や means room temperature, not chilled.
sol_flags.suggestion: Use “吟醸酒を冷やして飲む: to drink ginjo sake chilled,” or translate the existing phrase as “to drink ginjo sake at room temperature.”

decisions.note: junmai not with honjozo; 冷や is room temp

definitions.gloss: ginjo sake; premium sake brewed from highly polished rice
definitions.explanation: A grade of Japanese sake made from rice that has been polished to remove at least 40% of the outer layer. Known for its fruity aroma and clean, refined flavor.

examples.japanese: {吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧⟦{頼|たの}んだ→頼む：01104_tanomu⟧。
examples.english: I ordered a bottle of ginjo sake.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{華|はな}やか→華やか：06070_hanayaka⟧な⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: This ginjo sake has an elegant aroma.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冷|ひ}やした→冷やす：02403_hiyasu⟧{吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{刺身|さしみ}→刺身：04023_sashimi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{相性|あいしょう}→相性：13654_aishou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{抜群|ばつぐん}→抜群：12783_batsugun⟧だ。
examples.english: Chilled ginjo sake pairs exceptionally well with sashimi.

entry.notes:
One of the special designation grades ({特定名称酒|とくていめいしょうしゅ}) of Japanese sake. ⟦{吟醸|ぎんじょう}→吟醸：25617_ginjou⟧ means 'carefully brewed,' and the classification requires a rice polishing ratio ({精米歩合|せいまいぶあい}) of 60% or less (meaning 40% or more of each grain is polished away). The extensive polishing removes proteins and fats, resulting in a lighter, more fragrant sake.

TYPES:
The main grades, by how much the rice is polished:
- {大吟醸酒|だいぎんじょうしゅ}: daiginjo — polished to 50% or less, the most premium
- {吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}: ginjo — polished to 60% or less
- {本醸造酒|ほんじょうぞうしゅ}: honjozo — polished to 70% or less
- {純米|じゅんまい}: junmai — pure rice, no added alcohol (can be combined with the above)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {純米吟醸|じゅんまいぎんじょう}: junmai ginjo — ginjo sake made only from rice, water, and koji
- ⟦{吟醸|ぎんじょう}→吟醸：25617_ginjou⟧{香|か}: ginjo aroma — the characteristic fruity scent
- {吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{冷|ひ}や→冷や：28141_hiya⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧: to drink ginjo sake chilled

CULTURAL NOTE:
{吟醸酒|ぎんじょうしゅ} is best served chilled to preserve its delicate aroma. It became popular in the 1980s and helped transform the image of sake from a rustic drink to a refined beverage.

sol_flags.concern: Not all ores are minerals. Ore can be rock containing economically extractable minerals, whereas 鉱物 refers to minerals themselves.
sol_flags.suggestion: Replace with: "- 鉱物: mineral — a naturally occurring substance; ore is rock or mineral material from which valuable constituents can be extracted economically"

decisions.note: not all ores are minerals

definitions.gloss: ore; mineral ore
definitions.explanation: Rock or mineral from which metal or valuable minerals can be extracted. A key term in mining and geology.

examples.japanese: {鉱石|こうせき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{採掘|さいくつ}→採掘：07996_saikutsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{鉄|てつ}→鉄：02225_tetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{鉱石|こうせき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{取|と}れる→取れる：02376_toreru⟧。

examples.english: Many countries depend on importing ore.

examples.japanese: {鉱石|こうせき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{精錬|せいれん}→精錬：21301_seiren⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{金属|きんぞく}→金属：02645_kinzoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}り{出|だ}す→取り出す：04220_toridasu⟧。
examples.english: Metals are extracted by refining ore.

entry.notes:
Compound of {鉱|こう} (mine/mineral) and {石|せき} (stone). A fundamental term in geology, mining, and industry. Japan historically imported most of its ore, making {鉱石|こうせき} a common word in discussions of trade and resources.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉄鉱石|てっこうせき}: iron ore
- {銅鉱石|どうこうせき}: copper ore
- {鉱石|こうせき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{採掘|さいくつ}→採掘：07996_saikutsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to mine ore
- {鉱石|こうせき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{精錬|せいれん}→精錬：21301_seiren⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to refine ore
- {鉱石|こうせき}⟦ラジオ→ラジオ：01541_rajio⟧: crystal radio — a simple radio receiver using a crystal detector

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{鉱物|こうぶつ}→鉱物：04149_koubutsu⟧: mineral — a broader category; all ores are minerals but not all minerals are ores
- ⟦{宝石|ほうせき}→宝石：03619_houseki⟧: gemstone; jewel — a precious or decorative stone, different purpose than ore
- {原石|げんせき}: raw stone; uncut gem — an unprocessed stone, especially a gemstone before cutting

entry.gloss: time deposit; fixed-term deposit; term savings

entry.gloss: delivery; something delivered; gift sent to someone

definitions.gloss: delivery; something delivered; gift sent to someone
definitions.explanation: An item that is delivered or sent to someone, often a gift or package. Implies a personal or thoughtful delivery rather than commercial shipping.

examples.japanese: {届|とど}け{物|もの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{届|とど}いた→届く：00899_todoku⟧。
examples.english: A delivery arrived.
I made a delivery to the neighboring house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{届|とど}け{物|もの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{届|とど}いた→届く：00899_todoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{中身|なかみ}→中身：01483_nakami⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{確認|かくにん}した→確認する：25332_kakuninsuru⟧。
examples.english: A package arrived from my mother, so I checked what was inside.

entry.notes:
Refers to something delivered to a person, often with a nuance of personal care or thoughtfulness. While ⟦{荷物|にもつ}→荷物：00737_nimotsu⟧ is a neutral word for a package or parcel, {届|とど}け{物|もの} suggests something specifically intended for the recipient.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {届|とど}け{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to make a delivery
- {届|とど}け{物|もの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{届|とど}く→届く：00899_todoku⟧: a delivery arrives
- {届|とど}け{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{預|あず}かる→預かる：01817_azukaru⟧: to hold a delivery (for someone)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{荷物|にもつ}→荷物：00737_nimotsu⟧: package, parcel — neutral term for any shipped item
- ⟦{贈|おく}り{物|もの}→贈り物：01343_okurimono⟧: gift — emphasizes the gift-giving aspect
- {届|とど}け{物|もの} falls between the two, covering both deliveries and personal gifts sent to someone

FORMS:
⟦{届|とど}ける→届ける：01248_todokeru⟧ (to deliver) + ⟦{物|もの}→物：02259_mono⟧ (thing)

entry.gloss: family; clan; school (of an art or discipline)

definitions.gloss: family; clan; lineage
definitions.explanation: A family group or clan sharing a common ancestor or family name. Often used in historical or formal contexts.

definitions.gloss: school; group of disciples (in an art or discipline)
definitions.explanation: A group of practitioners or disciples under one master, especially in traditional arts like sumo, rakugo, tea ceremony, or martial arts.

examples.japanese: {平家|へいけ}{一門|いちもん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{滅|ほろ}んだ→滅ぶ：31716_horobu⟧。

examples.english: To join a master's school.
This school has many disciples.

examples.japanese: ⟦{落語|らくご}→落語：04457_rakugo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一門|いちもん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入門|にゅうもん}→入門：11643_nyuumon⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{修行|しゅぎょう}→修行：05522_shugyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。

entry.notes:
Refers to a group united by blood ties or by a shared master in a traditional discipline. The word carries a sense of loyalty and shared identity.

SENSE 1 — CLAN/FAMILY:
Common in historical contexts, especially referring to warrior clans of medieval Japan such as {平家|へいけ}{一門|いちもん} (Taira clan) or ⟦{源氏|げんじ}→源氏：16644_genji⟧{一門|いちもん} (Minamoto clan).

SENSE 2 — SCHOOL/GROUP:
Widely used in traditional arts:
- ⟦{相撲|すもう}→相撲：00390_sumou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一門|いちもん}: sumo stable group
- ⟦{落語|らくご}→落語：04457_rakugo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一門|いちもん}: rakugo school
- ⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一門|いちもん}: tea ceremony school

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一門|いちもん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧: to join a school/clan
- {一門|いちもん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{長|おさ}: head of a clan/school
- {一門|いちもん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{率|ひき}いる→率いる：10879_hikiiru⟧: to lead a clan/school

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{一族|いちぞく}→一族：11229_ichizoku⟧: family, relatives — focuses on blood relations
- ⟦{門下|もんか}→門下：23488_monka⟧: disciples under a master — focuses on the student-teacher relationship
- ⟦{流派|りゅうは}→流派：13365_ryuuha⟧: school of art — refers to the style or tradition itself

definitions.explanation: A musical time signature with three beats per measure, as in a waltz.

Has both a literal musical meaning and a widely used figurative meaning referring to three ideal qualities.

SENSE 2 — FIGURATIVE:
The key expression is {三拍子|さんびょうし}⟦{揃|そろ}う→揃う：01953_sorou⟧ (to have all three qualities aligned). This is used as high praise, meaning someone or something excels in three key areas simultaneously. The three qualities vary by context but are typically stated or implied.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三拍子|さんびょうし}⟦{揃|そろ}う→揃う：01953_sorou⟧: to have all three qualities
- {三拍子|さんびょうし}⟦{揃|そろ}った→揃う：01953_sorou⟧: having the complete package
- {三拍子|さんびょうし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦リズム→リズム：04746_rizumu⟧: triple-time rhythm

FORMS:
⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧ (three) + {拍子|びょうし} (beat, rhythm)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {四拍子|よんびょうし}: quadruple time — musical only, no figurative use
- {拍子|びょうし}: beat, rhythm — the base word

definitions.gloss: collection; recovery (of debts or payments)
definitions.explanation: The act of collecting money owed, especially debts. Can imply aggressive or persistent collection efforts.

examples.english: Freshly picked vegetables are delicious.

examples.japanese: {取|と}り{立|た}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{刺身|さしみ}→刺身：04023_sashimi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。

entry.notes:
Has two distinct meanings that are easily distinguished by context. Sense 1 (debt collection) appears in financial and legal contexts, while sense 2 (freshness) appears with food and agricultural products.

SENSE 1 — COLLECTION:
- {取|と}り{立|た}て⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧: debt collector
- {取|と}り{立|た}て⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧: the collector comes
- ⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧{取|と}り{立|た}て: harsh collection

SENSE 2 — FRESHNESS:
Used as a modifier before nouns with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧: {取|と}り{立|た}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧, {取|と}り{立|た}て⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{卵|たまご}→卵：02222_tamago⟧. This sense is always positive, emphasizing just-harvested quality.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{回収|かいしゅう}→回収：03019_kaishuu⟧: recovery, collection — more formal, broader usage
- ⟦{新鮮|しんせん}→新鮮：03261_shinsen⟧: fresh — describes the quality itself, not the act of harvesting
- {採|と}れたて: freshly harvested — similar to sense 2 but more casual

FORMS:
{取|と}り{立|た}てる (to collect; to appoint) → {取|と}り{立|た}て (noun form)

entry.gloss: Japanese rendering of classical Chinese text (kanbun)

definitions.gloss: Japanese rendering of classical Chinese text; kanbun written in Japanese word order
definitions.explanation: A version of a classical Chinese (kanbun) text that has been rearranged into Japanese word order and supplemented with Japanese grammatical elements, making it readable as Japanese prose.

examples.japanese: ⟦{漢文|かんぶん}→漢文：13398_kanbun⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To render classical Chinese into Japanese reading order.

examples.japanese: {書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んで→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{考|かんが}える→考える：00856_kangaeru⟧。
examples.english: To read the Japanese rendering and think about the meaning.

examples.japanese: ⟦{高校|こうこう}→高校：01083_koukou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{国語|こくご}→国語：02739_kokugo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{漢文|かんぶん}→漢文：13398_kanbun⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{変換|へんかん}する→変換する：09890_henkansuru⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In high school Japanese class, we practiced converting kanbun into Japanese-order renderings.

entry.notes:
A term from classical Japanese education. In kanbun study, the original Chinese text is first annotated with reading marks (⟦{返|かえ}り{点|てん}→返り点：31561_kaeriten⟧ and ⟦{送|おく}り{仮名|がな}→送り仮名：15047_okurigana⟧), then rewritten as {書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん} — a version readable as Japanese.

RELATED WORDS:
The stages of reading a kanbun text:
1. {白文|はくぶん}: the original Chinese text without annotations
2. ⟦{訓読|くんどく}→訓読：18554_kundoku⟧⟦{文|ぶん}→文：03716_bun⟧: text with reading marks added
3. {書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}: the full Japanese-order rendering
4. {現代語訳|げんだいごやく}: modern Japanese translation

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to render into Japanese reading order
- {書|か}き{下|くだ}し{文|ぶん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{直|なお}す: to convert to Japanese reading order

USAGE:
This term is encountered mainly in ⟦{国語|こくご}→国語：02739_kokugo⟧ (Japanese language) education at the high school level, where students study ⟦{漢文|かんぶん}→漢文：13398_kanbun⟧ (classical Chinese texts) as part of the curriculum.

entry.gloss: to rest one's elbows on (a table); to prop one's chin on one's elbow

definitions.explanation: The action of placing one's elbows on a surface such as a table. In Japanese culture, this is generally considered bad manners, especially while eating.

entry.notes:
A common expression in daily life, especially in conversations about table manners and etiquette. In Japanese culture, putting elbows on the table is considered rude, particularly during meals.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦テーブル→テーブル：04488_teeburu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{肘|ひじ}をつく: to put elbows on the table

Parents often scold children with 「{肘|ひじ}をつくな」(don't put your elbows on the table). This is one of the basic rules of Japanese table etiquette, alongside not sticking chopsticks upright in rice.

entry.gloss: traditional age counting; East Asian age reckoning

definitions.gloss: traditional age counting; East Asian age reckoning
definitions.explanation: A traditional system of counting age in which a person is one year old at birth and gains a year every New Year's Day, rather than on their birthday.

examples.japanese: {数|かぞ}え{年|どし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧{三十歳|さんじゅっさい}だ。
examples.english: In traditional age counting, I am thirty this year.

examples.japanese: ⟦{七五三|しちごさん}→七五三：06185_shichigosan⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{数|かぞ}え{年|どし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{祝|いわ}う→祝う：01881_iwau⟧⟦{家庭|かてい}→家庭：12315_katei⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Some families celebrate Shichi-Go-San based on traditional age counting.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{数|かぞ}え{年|どし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一般的|いっぱんてき}→一般的：04784_ippanteki⟧だった⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{満年齢|まんねんれい}→満年齢：23904_mannenrei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{使|つか}われている→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: In the past, traditional age counting was common, but now the Western system is used.

entry.notes:
Under this system, a baby is considered one year old ({一歳|いっさい}) at birth, and everyone becomes one year older on January 1st (originally based on the lunar new year). This means a person born on December 31st would be considered two years old on the following day.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {数|かぞ}え{年|どし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧: in traditional age counting
- {数|かぞ}え{年|どし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{年齢|ねんれい}→年齢：01490_nenrei⟧: age by traditional reckoning
- {数|かぞ}え{年|どし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{祝|いわ}う→祝う：01881_iwau⟧: to celebrate by traditional age

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{満年齢|まんねんれい}→満年齢：23904_mannenrei⟧: Western-style age — counting from birthday to birthday, which is the standard system in modern Japan

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan officially switched to the Western age system (⟦{満年齢|まんねんれい}→満年齢：23904_mannenrei⟧) in 1950, but {数|かぞ}え{年|どし} is still used for some traditional events like ⟦{厄年|やくどし}→厄年：05809_yakudoshi⟧ (unlucky years) and ⟦{還暦|かんれき}→還暦：05807_kanreki⟧ (60th birthday celebration).

definitions.gloss: loss by default; forfeit
definitions.explanation: A loss recorded in a competition when a participant cannot compete, whether due to injury, absence, or disqualification, without an actual match taking place.

examples.japanese: {怪我|けが}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{不戦敗|ふせんぱい}になった。
examples.english: I lost by default due to an injury.

examples.japanese: ⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{来|こ}なかった→来る：00254_kuru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{不戦敗|ふせんぱい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The opposing team didn't show up, so it was a forfeit.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大関|おおぜき}→大関：12662_oozeki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{体調不良|たいちょうふりょう}→体調不良：20233_taichoufuryou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{休場|きゅうじょう}し、⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{取組|とりくみ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{不戦敗|ふせんぱい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The ōzeki withdrew due to poor health, and today's bout was recorded as a loss by default.

entry.notes:
Compound of ⟦{不戦|ふせん}→不戦：24628_fusen⟧ (without fighting) and {敗|はい} (defeat). Commonly used in sumo, martial arts, and other competitive sports. The opposite is ⟦{不戦勝|ふせんしょう}→不戦勝：08409_fusenshou⟧ (win by default).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不戦敗|ふせんぱい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to lose by default
- {不戦敗|ふせんぱい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{付|つ}く→付く：01960_tsuku⟧: to have a default loss recorded
- {不戦敗|ふせんぱい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{喫|きっ}する→喫する：29124_kissuru⟧: to suffer a forfeit loss

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{不戦勝|ふせんしょう}→不戦勝：08409_fusenshou⟧: win by default — the counterpart; a win without fighting
- ⟦{棄権|きけん}→棄権：16194_kiken⟧: withdrawal, abstention — the act of withdrawing from a competition, which often causes a {不戦敗|ふせんぱい}
- ⟦{反則負|はんそくま}け→反則負け：22305_hansokumake⟧: loss by foul — losing due to a rule violation during an actual match

definitions.gloss: loss by foul; disqualification loss
definitions.explanation: A loss in a competition resulting from committing a foul or rules violation, rather than being outperformed.

examples.japanese: {反則負|はんそくま}けになった。
examples.english: He lost by disqualification.

examples.japanese: ⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧な⟦{技|わざ}→技：02172_waza⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}って→使う：00473_tsukau⟧{反則負|はんそくま}け⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: He was disqualified for using a dangerous technique.

examples.japanese: ⟦{横綱|よこづな}→横綱：14957_yokozuna⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{髷|まげ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧つかんだ⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧{反則負|はんそくま}け⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{宣告|せんこく}→宣告：06819_senkoku⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The yokozuna was declared the loser by foul for grabbing his opponent's topknot.

entry.notes:
Compound of ⟦{反則|はんそく}→反則：06541_hansoku⟧ (foul, violation) and ⟦{負|ま}け→負け：02569_make⟧ (loss, defeat). Most commonly associated with sumo, judo, and other martial arts, but applicable to any competitive sport.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {反則負|はんそくま}け⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to lose by foul
- {反則負|はんそくま}け⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{宣告|せんこく}→宣告：06819_senkoku⟧⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧: to be declared a loss by foul
- {反則負|はんそくま}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: (of a referee) to call a disqualification loss

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{不戦敗|ふせんぱい}→不戦敗：22302_fusenpai⟧: loss by default — losing without competing, due to absence or withdrawal
- {反則勝|はんそくが}ち: win by opponent's foul — the counterpart; winning because the opponent committed a foul
- ⟦{失格|しっかく}→失格：12195_shikkaku⟧: disqualification — a broader term for being removed from competition entirely

sol_flags.concern: 敬白 is not exclusively paired with 謹啓; it can also close letters beginning with other highly formal openings, such as 恭啓.
sol_flags.suggestion: Replace with: "Commonly paired with the opening 謹啓."

decisions.note: not always with 謹啓

entry.gloss: respectfully yours; yours sincerely (closing word of a letter)

definitions.gloss: respectfully yours; yours sincerely
definitions.explanation: A formal closing phrase used at the end of a letter, paired with the opening {謹啓|きんけい}. More formal than {敬具|けいぐ}.

examples.japanese: ⟦{謹啓|きんけい}→謹啓：22309_kinkei⟧…{敬白|けいはく}。
examples.english: Dear Sir/Madam ... Respectfully yours.

examples.japanese: ⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{敬白|けいはく}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{書|か}いた→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: I wrote 'respectfully yours' at the end of the letter.

examples.japanese: ⟦{式典|しきてん}→式典：09526_shikiten⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{招待状|しょうたいじょう}→招待状：14769_shoutaijou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{謹啓|きんけい}→謹啓：22309_kinkei⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{始|はじ}まり→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧{敬白|けいはく}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{結|むす}ぶ→結ぶ：02308_musubu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{正式|せいしき}→正式：03376_seishiki⟧だ。
examples.english: The formal way to write a ceremony invitation is to begin with 'respectfully' and close with 'sincerely yours.'

sol_flags.concern: 敬白 is not the only closing used with 謹啓; 謹言 and 謹白 are also standard pairings.
sol_flags.suggestion: Replace with "Commonly paired with closings such as 敬白, 謹言, or 謹白." Also remove the exclusive pairing claim from the definition's explanation.

decisions.note: 謹言 and 謹白 also pair

entry.gloss: respectfully (opening word of a letter); Dear Sir or Madam

definitions.gloss: respectfully; with great respect (formal letter opening)
definitions.explanation: A highly formal opening phrase used at the beginning of a letter. Literally means 'I respectfully state.' Always paired with the closing {敬白|けいはく}.

examples.japanese: {謹啓|きんけい}　{時下|じか}⟦ますます→ますます：01604_masumasu⟧ご{清栄|せいえい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧こととお⟦{喜|よろこ}び→喜び：03672_yorokobi⟧⟦{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます→申し上げる：01734_moushiageru⟧。
examples.english: Dear Sir/Madam, I trust you are enjoying continued prosperity.

examples.japanese: ⟦{正式|せいしき}→正式：03376_seishiki⟧な⟦{文書|ぶんしょ}→文書：12947_bunsho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{謹啓|きんけい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: Use 'kinkei' in formal documents.

examples.japanese: ⟦{結婚式|けっこんしき}→結婚式：05493_kekkonshiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{招待状|しょうたいじょう}→招待状：14769_shoutaijou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{謹啓|きんけい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}き{始|はじ}める→書き始める：22272_kakihajimeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一般的|いっぱんてき}→一般的：04784_ippanteki⟧だ。
examples.english: It is standard to begin wedding invitations with 'kinkei.'

entry.notes:
The most formal of the standard letter-opening phrases. Composed of {謹|きん} (respectfully) and {啓|けい} (to state, to inform). Used in highly formal contexts such as wedding invitations, corporate announcements, and official correspondence. Must be paired with the closing ⟦{敬白|けいはく}→敬白：22308_keihaku⟧.

RELATED WORDS (by formality):
- {前略|ぜんりゃく} / {草々|そうそう}: informal
- ⟦{拝啓|はいけい}→拝啓：12790_haikei⟧ / ⟦{敬具|けいぐ}→敬具：12977_keigu⟧: standard formal
- {謹啓|きんけい} / ⟦{敬白|けいはく}→敬白：22308_keihaku⟧: highly formal

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{拝啓|はいけい}→拝啓：12790_haikei⟧: Dear Sir/Madam — the standard formal opening; less formal than {謹啓|きんけい}
- {前略|ぜんりゃく}: (dispensing with formalities) — a casual opening that skips the seasonal greeting
- ⟦{敬白|けいはく}→敬白：22308_keihaku⟧: respectfully yours — the corresponding closing for {謹啓|きんけい}

definitions.gloss: running; jogging; double time
definitions.explanation: Running at a quick pace, faster than walking but not necessarily sprinting. Often used as a command in military or gym contexts.

definitions.gloss: hurried; rushed; quick overview
definitions.explanation: Doing something in a hurried manner, often skipping details. Commonly used figuratively to describe a brief or superficial treatment of a topic.

examples.japanese: {駆|か}け{足|あし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{走|はし}る→走る：00519_hashiru⟧。
examples.english: To run at a quick pace.

examples.japanese: ⟦{集合|しゅうごう}→集合：03068_shuugou⟧⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{遅|おく}れ→遅れる：00741_okureru⟧そうで、{駆|か}け{足|あし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{向|む}かった→向かう：01186_mukau⟧。
examples.english: I was about to be late for the meeting time, so I headed there at a run.

examples.japanese: ⟦{体育|たいいく}→体育：03384_taiiku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{校庭|こうてい}→校庭：04147_koutei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{駆|か}け{足|あし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧{周|しゅう}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In gym class, we ran three laps around the schoolyard at a jog.

examples.japanese: {駆|か}け{足|あし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{説明|せつめい}する→説明する：05639_setsumeisuru⟧。
examples.english: To give a quick overview.

examples.japanese: ⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{駆|か}け{足|あし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{紹介|しょうかい}します→紹介する：05641_shoukaisuru⟧。
examples.english: Since we're short on time, I'll give a quick introduction.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{駆|か}け{足|あし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{振|ふ}り{返|かえ}って→振り返る：04231_furikaeru⟧みましょう。
examples.english: Let's take a quick look back through Japanese history.

entry.notes:
A compound of ⟦{駆|か}ける→駆ける：14714_kakeru⟧ (to run/gallop) + ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧ (foot/pace). Has both a literal physical meaning and a very common figurative meaning of doing something hastily or in abbreviated fashion.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {駆|か}け{足|あし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{回|まわ}る→回る：01150_mawaru⟧: to rush through (sightseeing, etc.)
- {駆|か}け{足|あし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{説明|せつめい}する→説明する：05639_setsumeisuru⟧: to explain quickly
- {駆|か}け{足|あし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{紹介|しょうかい}する→紹介する：05641_shoukaisuru⟧: to give a quick introduction
- {駆|か}け{足|あし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{旅|たび}→旅：03407_tabi⟧: a whirlwind trip

USAGE:
The figurative sense (sense 2) is used adverbially with で, meaning "in a rushed manner." This usage is extremely common in presentations, lectures, and guided tours where time is limited.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{小走|こばし}り→小走り：21117_kobashiri⟧: light jog/trot — physical running only, no figurative use
- {急|いそ}ぎ{足|あし}: hurried pace — walking quickly, not running

definitions.gloss: horse racing ticket; betting slip; racing bet
definitions.explanation: A ticket purchased to bet on horse races, representing a wager on which horse or combination of horses will win, place, or show. Horse racing is one of the few forms of legal gambling in Japan.

examples.english: To buy a horse racing ticket.

examples.japanese: {馬券|ばけん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{当|あ}たって→当たる：01860_ataru⟧⟦{大喜|おおよろこ}び→大喜び：28880_ooyorokobi⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I was overjoyed when my racing bet won.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎週|まいしゅう}→毎週：00730_maishuu⟧⟦{日曜日|にちようび}→日曜日：00656_nichiyoubi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{競馬場|けいばじょう}→競馬場：31242_keibajou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}って→行く：00119_iku⟧{馬券|ばけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{楽|たの}しみ→楽しみ：01651_tanoshimi⟧だ。
examples.english: My father's weekly pleasure is going to the racetrack on Sundays to buy betting tickets.

entry.notes:
Composed of {馬|ば} (horse) + ⟦{券|けん}→券：02150_ken⟧ (ticket/voucher). Formally called {勝馬投票券|かちうまとうひょうけん} (winning horse voting ticket). Horse racing (⟦{競馬|けいば}→競馬：00207_keiba⟧) is one of the major forms of legalized gambling in Japan, along with bicycle racing, boat racing, and motorcycle racing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {馬券|ばけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧: to buy a racing ticket
- {馬券|ばけん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{当|あ}たる→当たる：01860_ataru⟧: to win on a racing bet
- {馬券|ばけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{外|はず}す→外す：02394_hazusu⟧: to lose a racing bet
- {馬券|ばけん}⟦{売|う}り{場|ば}→売り場：01331_uriba⟧: ticket-selling area at a racetrack

TYPES:
Common bet types:
- {単勝|たんしょう}: win (picking the first-place horse)
- {複勝|ふくしょう}: place (picking a top-three horse)
- {馬連|うまれん}: quinella (picking first and second in any order)
- {三連単|さんれんたん}: trifecta (first, second, third in exact order)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Horse racing is regulated by the JRA (⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦{中央|ちゅうおう}→中央：03475_chuuou⟧{競馬会|けいばかい}) and local governments. {馬券|ばけん} can be purchased at racetracks, off-track betting facilities, and online.

definitions.gloss: under construction; being built
definitions.explanation: The state of a building, road, or other structure currently being constructed. Commonly seen on signs at construction sites.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{道路|どうろ}→道路：01481_douro⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{建設中|けんせつちゅう}です。
examples.english: This road is under construction.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{建設中|けんせつちゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{高層|こうそう}ビル→高層ビル：16994_kousoubiru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There is a high-rise building under construction in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {新|しん}⟦スタジアム→スタジアム：23905_sutajiamu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{現在|げんざい}→現在：01556_genzai⟧{建設中|けんせつちゅう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{来年|らいねん}→来年：00745_rainen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{完成|かんせい}→完成：01550_kansei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{目指|めざ}している→目指す：10528_mezasu⟧。
examples.english: The new stadium is currently under construction, aiming for completion next year.

entry.notes:
Composed of ⟦{建設|けんせつ}→建設：02708_kensetsu⟧ (construction/building) + ⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧ (during/in the middle of). RELATED WORDS:

definitions.gloss: prize money; reward; bounty
definitions.explanation: Money offered as a prize for winning a contest or competition, or as a reward for information or the capture of a wanted person.

examples.japanese: {懸賞金|けんしょうきん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{百万|ひゃくまん}→百万：08109_hyakuman⟧⟦{円|えん}→円：00774_en⟧です。
examples.english: The prize money is one million yen.

examples.japanese: ⟦{犯人|はんにん}→犯人：03572_hannin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{懸賞金|けんしょうきん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧かけられた。
examples.english: A bounty was placed on the criminal.

examples.japanese: ⟦{情報|じょうほう}→情報：03348_jouhou⟧{提供者|ていきょうしゃ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{最大|さいだい}→最大：04827_saidai⟧{三百万|さんびゃくまん}⟦{円|えん}→円：00774_en⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{懸賞金|けんしょうきん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{支払|しはら}われる→支払う：02116_shiharau⟧ことになっている。
examples.english: An informant can receive up to three million yen in reward money.

entry.notes:
Composed of {懸賞|けんしょう} (prize/reward) + {金|きん} (money). Used in two main contexts: prize money for contests and competitions, and reward money for information leading to the capture of criminals.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {懸賞金|けんしょうきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かける→かける：00854_kakeru⟧: to put up a reward/bounty
- {懸賞金|けんしょうきん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: a reward is offered
- {懸賞金|けんしょうきん}⟦{付|つ}き→付き：26333_tsuki⟧: with a bounty attached
- {懸賞金|けんしょうきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}け{取|と}る→受け取る：01883_uketoru⟧: to receive the prize/reward money

SIMILAR WORDS:

- ⟦{報奨金|ほうしょうきん}→報奨金：18793_houshoukin⟧: incentive money/bonus — for good performance or tips
- {褒賞金|ほうしょうきん}: reward money — formal, from government or organizations

sol_flags.concern: 着地する means to land, not to dismount, and 平均台で does not mean 'from the balance beam.'

decisions.note: 着地 is land, not dismount

definitions.gloss: balance beam
definitions.explanation: A narrow, raised beam used in gymnastics. The gymnast performs acrobatic moves, jumps, and poses while balancing on the beam. Also found in school gym equipment.

examples.japanese: {平均台|へいきんだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
examples.english: To walk on the balance beam.

examples.japanese: {平均台|へいきんだい}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{落|お}ちて→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧しまった。
examples.english: I fell off the balance beam.

examples.japanese: ⟦オリンピック→オリンピック：09899_orinpikku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{体操|たいそう}{競技|きょうぎ}→体操競技：26394_taisoukyougi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{平均台|へいきんだい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{金|きん}メダル→金メダル：20781_kinmedaru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{獲得|かくとく}→獲得：05624_kakutoku⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: She won the gold medal on the balance beam at the Olympic gymnastics competition.

entry.notes:
Composed of ⟦{平均|へいきん}→平均：03614_heikin⟧ (balance/average) + {台|だい} (platform/stand). In competitive gymnastics, the balance beam is one of the four apparatus events for women. The beam is 10 cm wide and 125 cm off the ground.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {平均台|へいきんだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{演技|えんぎ}→演技：01890_engi⟧: balance beam routine
- {平均台|へいきんだい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{着地|ちゃくち}→着地：15276_chakuchi⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to dismount from the balance beam
- {平均台|へいきんだい}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{落|お}ちる→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧: to fall off the balance beam

RELATED WORDS:

- ⟦{鉄棒|てつぼう}→鉄棒：17912_tetsubou⟧: horizontal bar
- ⟦{床|ゆか}→床：03652_yuka⟧⟦{運動|うんどう}→運動：00821_undou⟧: floor exercise
- {鞍馬|あんば}: pommel horse
- ⟦{段違|だんちが}い→段違い：25270_danchigai⟧{平行棒|へいこうぼう}: uneven bars

definitions.gloss: to sterilize; to kill all microorganisms
definitions.explanation: To completely eliminate bacteria and other microorganisms from equipment, instruments, or materials. Used in medical, laboratory, and food safety contexts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{器具|きぐ}→器具：03980_kigu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{滅菌|めっきん}する。
examples.english: Sterilize the instruments.

examples.japanese: ⟦{手術|しゅじゅつ}→手術：03218_shujutsu⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{道具|どうぐ}→道具：01479_dougu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧すべて{滅菌|めっきん}し⟦なければならない→なければならない：27600_nakerebanaranai⟧。
examples.english: All tools must be sterilized before surgery.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}→牛乳：00777_gyuunyuu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{高温|こうおん}→高温：14705_kouon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{滅菌|めっきん}されて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で⟦{長期|ちょうき}{保存|ほぞん}→長期保存：18447_choukihozon⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: This milk has been sterilized at high temperature, so it can be stored for a long time.

entry.notes:
A technical term meaning complete elimination of microorganisms, stricter than ⟦{殺菌|さっきん}→殺菌：09781_sakkin⟧ (which reduces but may not eliminate all bacteria) or ⟦{消毒|しょうどく}→消毒：07591_shoudoku⟧ (disinfection).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{滅菌|めっきん}→滅菌：24175_mekkin⟧⟦{処理|しょり}→処理：03251_shori⟧: sterilization treatment
- ⟦{滅菌|めっきん}→滅菌：24175_mekkin⟧⟦{済|ず}み→〜済み：04013_zumi⟧: sterilized; already sterilized
- ⟦{高圧|こうあつ}→高圧：21094_kouatsu⟧⟦{蒸気|じょうき}→蒸気：04278_jouki⟧⟦{滅菌|めっきん}→滅菌：24175_mekkin⟧: autoclave sterilization
- ⟦{滅菌|めっきん}→滅菌：24175_mekkin⟧⟦ガーゼ→ガーゼ：28833_gaaze⟧: sterile gauze

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{殺菌|さっきん}→殺菌：09781_sakkin⟧: bactericidal treatment — reduces bacteria but does not guarantee complete elimination
- ⟦{消毒|しょうどく}→消毒：07591_shoudoku⟧: disinfection — removal of pathogens from surfaces, broader and less strict
- ⟦{除菌|じょきん}→除菌：07789_jokin⟧: sanitization — removal of bacteria, common in household product marketing

FORMS:
{滅|めつ} (destroy) + ⟦{菌|きん}→菌：02682_kin⟧ (bacteria). Literally 'destroy bacteria.'

sol_flags.concern: 注油する denotes the action of oiling or lubricating, not a tool.
sol_flags.suggestion: Remove the semantic tag "tool".

decisions.note: action, not tool

definitions.gloss: to oil; to lubricate; to apply oil
definitions.explanation: To apply oil or lubricant to machinery, hinges, chains, or other mechanical parts to reduce friction and ensure smooth operation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{自転車|じてんしゃ}→自転車：00633_jitensha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦チェーン→チェーン：08833_cheen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{注油|ちゅうゆ}する。
examples.english: Oil the bicycle chain.

examples.japanese: ⟦ドア→ドア：00773_doa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{蝶番|ちょうつがい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧きしむ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{注油|ちゅうゆ}した。
examples.english: The door hinges were squeaking, so I oiled them.

examples.japanese: ⟦{機械|きかい}→機械：02366_kikai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{寿命|じゅみょう}→寿命：12359_jumyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{延|の}ばす→延ばす：28291_nobasu⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{定期的|ていきてき}→定期的：06173_teikiteki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{注油|ちゅうゆ}すること⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧だ。
examples.english: To extend the life of machinery, it's important to lubricate it regularly.

entry.notes:
A practical term for the act of applying oil or lubricant to mechanical parts. Common in maintenance manuals, bicycle care, and industrial contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{注油|ちゅうゆ}→注油：18571_chuuyu⟧{口|ぐち}: oil fill port; lubrication point
- ⟦{定期的|ていきてき}→定期的：06173_teikiteki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{注油|ちゅうゆ}する: to oil regularly
- ⟦{注油|ちゅうゆ}→注油：18571_chuuyu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧: needs oiling

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{潤滑|じゅんかつ}→潤滑：23861_junkatsu⟧: lubrication — more technical term
- ⟦{油|あぶら}→油：01693_abura⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{差|さ}す→差す：17637_sasu⟧: to oil; to grease — everyday expression with the same meaning
- ⟦{給油|きゅうゆ}→給油：18553_kyuuyu⟧: refueling a car, plane or ship (in machinery manuals it can also mean supplying lubricating oil); ⟦{注油|ちゅうゆ}→注油：18571_chuuyu⟧ is only lubrication

FORMS:
⟦{注|ちゅう}→注：03434_chuu⟧ (pour) + {油|ゆ} (oil). Literally 'pour oil.'

entry.gloss: to disappear; to vanish; to become extinct

definitions.gloss: to disappear; to vanish; to cease to exist
definitions.explanation: To completely disappear from existence. Used for things that were once present but are now entirely gone, such as civilizations, species, rights, or physical phenomena.

examples.japanese: ⟦{権利|けんり}→権利：02711_kenri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{消滅|しょうめつ}する。
examples.english: The right expires.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{文明|ぶんめい}→文明：03611_bunmei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{千年前|せんねんまえ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{消滅|しょうめつ}した。
examples.english: That civilization vanished a thousand years ago.

examples.japanese: ⟦{地球|ちきゅう}{温暖化|おんだんか}→地球温暖化：18873_chikyuuondanka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{進|すす}めば→進む：01225_susumu⟧、{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{生物|せいぶつ}→生物：03295_seibutsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{消滅|しょうめつ}する{恐|おそ}れ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: If global warming continues, there is a risk that many species will become extinct.

entry.notes:
Describes something ceasing to exist entirely, not merely being hidden or temporarily absent. The disappearance is permanent and complete. Used in formal and written contexts more than in casual speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{権利|けんり}→権利：02711_kenri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{消滅|しょうめつ}する: a right expires
- {時効|じこう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{消滅|しょうめつ}する: the statute of limitations expires
- ⟦{文化|ぶんか}→文化：01504_bunka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{消滅|しょうめつ}する: a culture dies out
- ⟦{種|しゅ}→種：28584_shu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{消滅|しょうめつ}する: a species becomes extinct
- ⟦{消滅|しょうめつ}→消滅：13331_shoumetsu⟧⟦{危機|きき}→危機：11798_kiki⟧: danger of extinction

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{消|き}える→消える：02520_kieru⟧: to disappear — everyday word for something ceasing to be visible or present; less final
- ⟦{絶滅|ぜつめつ}→絶滅：03756_zetsumetsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to become extinct — specifically for species dying out completely
- ⟦{消失|しょうしつ}→消失：13351_shoushitsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to vanish / to be lost — emphasizes loss, often of something that should have remained
- ⟦{滅|ほろ}びる→滅びる：10881_horobiru⟧: to perish / to be destroyed — implies destruction or ruin of something large like a nation

REGISTER:
Formal. Common in legal, academic, and journalistic writing. In everyday speech, ⟦{消|き}える→消える：02520_kieru⟧ or なくなる are more natural.

sol_flags.concern: 印象的な can describe negative or disturbing things that leave a strong impression; it is not restricted to positive or neutral connotations.
sol_flags.suggestion: Replace with: "Describes something that creates a lasting impression, whether positive, neutral, or negative."

decisions.note: 印象的 can be negative

definitions.gloss: impressive; striking; memorable
definitions.explanation: Leaving a strong impression on the mind. Describes something that stands out and is not easily forgotten, whether because of its beauty, impact, or emotional resonance.

examples.japanese: {印象的|いんしょうてき}な⟦{場面|ばめん}→場面：03702_bamen⟧だった。
examples.english: It was a striking scene.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{笑顔|えがお}→笑顔：01884_egao⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧{印象的|いんしょうてき}だった。
examples.english: Her smile was very memorable.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧セリフ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧{印象的|いんしょうてき}だった⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{語|かた}っている→語る：01930_kataru⟧。
examples.english: Many people say the final line of the movie was the most memorable.

entry.notes:
Derived from ⟦{印象|いんしょう}→印象：01846_inshou⟧ (impression) + ⟦{的|てき}→〜的：09839_teki⟧ (adjectival suffix). Describes something that creates a lasting impression, always with a positive or neutral connotation — never used for negatively shocking things.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {印象的|いんしょうてき}な⟦{場面|ばめん}→場面：03702_bamen⟧: a striking scene
- {印象的|いんしょうてき}な⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧: memorable words
- {印象的|いんしょうてき}な⟦{出来事|できごと}→出来事：03446_dekigoto⟧: a memorable event
- {印象的|いんしょうてき}な⟦{演技|えんぎ}→演技：01890_engi⟧: an impressive performance
- ⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧{印象的|いんしょうてき}な: the most impressive/memorable

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{印象|いんしょう}→印象：01846_inshou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{残|のこ}る→残る：01187_nokoru⟧: to remain in one's memory — phrase with similar meaning but used as a verb
- ⟦{感動的|かんどうてき}→感動的：25931_kandouteki⟧な: moving / touching — stronger emotional impact, implies being deeply moved
- ⟦{衝撃的|しょうげきてき}→衝撃的：06829_shougekiteki⟧な: shocking / sensational — much stronger; implies surprise or shock
- ⟦{鮮|あざ}やか→鮮やか：05702_azayaka⟧な: vivid / brilliant — focuses on visual clarity and brightness

USAGE:
Can be used as an adverb with ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: {印象的|いんしょうてき}に⟦{描|えが}く→描く：02013_egaku⟧ (to portray impressively).

sol_flags.concern: Four tiers do not avoid the unlucky number four. The traditional avoidance concerns how the fourth tier is named.

sol_flags.concern: 弁当箱 are not necessarily single-compartment containers; they can have multiple compartments or stacking tiers.
sol_flags.suggestion: Replace with: "- 弁当箱: lunch box — a container for a packed meal, which may have compartments or stacking tiers"

definitions.gloss: tiered box; stacking food box; jubako
definitions.explanation: A set of square lacquered boxes that stack on top of each other, traditionally used for serving special occasion foods such as osechi (New Year dishes). Typically comes in sets of two to five tiers.

examples.japanese: {重箱|じゅうばこ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{詰|つ}める→詰める：02078_tsumeru⟧。

examples.japanese: {三段|さんだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{重箱|じゅうばこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{用意|ようい}した→用意する：22428_youisuru⟧。

examples.japanese: ⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{重箱|じゅうばこ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{詰|つ}めた→詰める：02078_tsumeru⟧⟦おせち{料理|りょうり}→おせち料理：26981_osechiryouri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{囲|かこ}む→囲む：02037_kakomu⟧。
examples.english: At New Year's, the whole family gathers around osechi dishes packed in tiered boxes.

entry.notes:
A traditional Japanese container consisting of stackable square boxes, usually lacquered. Most strongly associated with ⟦おせち{料理|りょうり}→おせち料理：26981_osechiryouri⟧ (New Year dishes) but also used for picnic foods and other special occasions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {重箱|じゅうばこ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{詰|つ}める→詰める：02078_tsumeru⟧: to pack into a tiered box
- {三段|さんだん}{重|じゅう}: three-tier box (abbreviated form)
- {重箱|じゅうばこ}{読|よ}み: jubako reading — a kanji compound read with on'yomi + kun'yomi (a linguistics term named after this word)
- {漆|うるし}{塗|ぬ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{重箱|じゅうばこ}: lacquered tiered box

CULTURAL NOTE:
The traditional number of tiers is five (or four, avoiding the unlucky number), though three-tier sets are most common today. Each tier of an ⟦おせち→おせち：09649_osechi⟧{重箱|じゅうばこ} traditionally holds specific types of dishes. The word also appears in the linguistic term {重箱|じゅうばこ}⟦{読|よ}み→読む：00426_yomu⟧, describing kanji compounds where the first character uses on'yomi and the second uses kun'yomi — just like {重|じゅう}(on) + {箱|ばこ}(kun).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{弁当箱|べんとうばこ}→弁当箱：20186_bentoubako⟧: lunch box — a single-compartment everyday container, unlike the stacking {重箱|じゅうばこ}

decisions.note: 発火点 is not flash point

definitions.gloss: ignition; catching fire; combustion
definitions.explanation: The act or event of something catching fire or beginning to burn. Can refer to both spontaneous combustion and deliberate ignition.

examples.japanese: {発火|はっか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There is a risk of ignition.

examples.japanese: ⟦バッテリー→バッテリー：04425_batterii⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{発火|はっか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{起|お}きた→起きる：00521_okiru⟧。

examples.japanese: ⟦{乾燥|かんそう}→乾燥：00184_kansou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{季節|きせつ}→季節：01304_kisetsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{枯|か}れ{葉|は}→枯れ葉：20386_kareha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧{発火|はっか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧だ。
examples.english: In dry seasons, dead leaves can spontaneously combust, so caution is needed.

entry.notes:
Describes the moment when something begins to burn. Often used in safety warnings and accident reports. The verb form {発火|はっか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ means "to catch fire" or "to ignite."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {発火|はっか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to catch fire / to ignite
- ⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧{発火|はっか}: spontaneous combustion
- {発火|はっか}{点|てん}: ignition point / flash point
- {発火|はっか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{原因|げんいん}→原因：01400_genin⟧: cause of ignition
- {発火|はっか}⟦{装置|そうち}→装置：03318_souchi⟧: ignition device
- {発火|はっか}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{危険|きけん}→危険：01141_kiken⟧: risk of catching fire

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {着火|ちゃっか}: ignition — very similar, but often implies intentional lighting; {発火|はっか} is more often spontaneous
- ⟦{点火|てんか}→点火：16200_tenka⟧: lighting a fire — deliberately setting fire to something (a stove, fireworks, etc.)
- ⟦{出火|しゅっか}→出火：20260_shukka⟧: outbreak of fire — the start of a fire as an incident, used in fire investigations
- ⟦{火災|かさい}→火災：02561_kasai⟧: fire (as a disaster) — the resulting fire event, not the moment of ignition

definitions.gloss: renting a room (in someone's house); subletting; lodging
definitions.explanation: Renting a room within someone else's home or existing space, rather than renting an entire apartment or house. Can also refer to borrowing part of a commercial space.

examples.japanese: {間借|まが}り⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{暮|く}らしている→暮らす：01937_kurasu⟧。

examples.japanese: ⟦{知人|ちじん}→知人：04056_chijin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{間借|まが}り⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。

entry.notes:
Describes renting part of a space, not the whole unit. Traditionally refers to renting a room in someone's home, a common arrangement in older Japan and still seen today. Recently also used for businesses sharing commercial space (e.g., a pop-up restaurant operating inside another restaurant's space).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {間借|まが}り⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to rent a room / to sublet
- {間借|まが}り⟦{人|にん}→〜人：00658_nin⟧: lodger / tenant

- {間借|まが}り⟦カレー→カレー：02898_karee⟧: pop-up curry restaurant (operating inside another space)
- {間借|まが}り⟦{営業|えいぎょう}→営業：01878_eigyou⟧: operating out of a shared/borrowed space

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{下宿|げしゅく}→下宿：01399_geshuku⟧: boarding house / lodging — a house specifically set up to take in boarders, with meals often included
- ⟦{賃貸|ちんたい}→賃貸：06081_chintai⟧: rental — renting an entire apartment or house
- ⟦{同居|どうきょ}→同居：09730_doukyo⟧: living together — sharing a home, but implies a closer relationship

USAGE:
The term {間借|まが}り has gained new life in the food industry, where {間借|まが}り⟦{営業|えいぎょう}→営業：01878_eigyou⟧ refers to a restaurant operating inside another establishment's space during off-hours, a popular low-cost way to start a food business.

sol_flags.concern: The characters in 真面目 were not chosen for their sounds to spell まじめ. This is a meaning-based spelling with a special whole-word reading.
sol_flags.suggestion: Replace with: "真面目 read as まじめ is a meaning-based spelling with a whole-word reading (熟字訓), rather than a combination of the characters’ usual readings."

decisions.note: 真面目 is jukujikun, not ateji

definitions.gloss: serious; earnest; diligent; sincere
definitions.explanation: Describes a person who is honest, hardworking, and takes things seriously. A highly valued trait in Japanese society, suggesting reliability and conscientiousness.

definitions.gloss: serious; not joking; genuine
definitions.explanation: Describes a tone, expression, or manner that is sincere and not playful or humorous.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{真面目|まじめ}な⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧だ。
examples.english: He is a serious person.

examples.japanese: {真面目|まじめ}に⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧⟦{姿|すがた}→姿：03363_sugata⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{評価|ひょうか}→評価：03583_hyouka⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Her diligent work attitude was appreciated.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{真面目|まじめ}な⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{約束|やくそく}→約束：01517_yakusoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{必|かなら}ず→必ず：01249_kanarazu⟧⟦{守|まも}る→守る：01986_mamoru⟧。
examples.english: She has an earnest personality and always keeps her promises.

examples.japanese: {真面目|まじめ}な⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To put on a serious face.

examples.japanese: {真面目|まじめ}な⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: I have something serious to talk about.

examples.japanese: 「⟦{冗談|じょうだん}→冗談：03347_joudan⟧でしょう？」「いや、{真面目|まじめ}に⟦{言|い}っている→言う：00515_iu⟧んだ。」
examples.english: "You're joking, right?" "No, I'm being serious."

entry.notes:
One of the most commonly used personality descriptors in Japanese. Being ⟦{真面目|まじめ}→真面目：01206_majime⟧ is generally seen as a positive trait, suggesting someone you can rely on. However, it can sometimes carry a slightly negative nuance of being too rigid, boring, or unable to relax.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {真面目|まじめ}な⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: a serious/earnest person
- {真面目|まじめ}な⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧: a serious personality
- {真面目|まじめ}に⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧: to work diligently
- {真面目|まじめ}な⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧: a serious talk
- {真面目|まじめ}な⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧: a serious expression
- {真面目|まじめ}に⟦{取|と}り{組|く}む→取り組む：04225_torikumu⟧: to tackle something seriously

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{誠実|せいじつ}→誠実：14211_seijitsu⟧な: sincere / faithful — more formal, emphasizes moral integrity
- ⟦{勤勉|きんべん}→勤勉：10145_kinben⟧な: diligent / industrious — specifically about hard work and study
- ⟦{几帳面|きちょうめん}→几帳面：06868_kichoumen⟧な: meticulous / precise — emphasizes attention to detail and orderliness
- ⟦{堅|かた}い→堅い：18753_katai⟧: stiff / rigid — can overlap with the "too serious" nuance of ⟦{真面目|まじめ}→真面目：01206_majime⟧

WRITING:
Also commonly written in hiragana as まじめ. The kanji ⟦{真面目|まじめ}→真面目：01206_majime⟧ is an example of ateji (kanji chosen for sound rather than meaning).

sol_flags.concern: 頑張ったなのに is ungrammatical: のに attaches directly to the past-tense verb 頑張った, without な.
sol_flags.suggestion: Replace 頑張ったなのに... with 頑張ったのに..., or use a valid なのに example such as 約束した日なのに....

entry.gloss: despite that; even though; and yet

definitions.gloss: despite that; even though; and yet; but
definitions.explanation: A conjunction expressing that the result or situation in the second clause is contrary to what would be expected from the first clause. Often carries a tone of frustration, disappointment, or surprise.

examples.japanese: ⟦{約束|やくそく}→約束：01517_yakusoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧なのに、⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{来|こ}なかった→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
examples.english: It was the day we had agreed on, and yet he didn't come.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日曜日|にちようび}→日曜日：00656_nichiyoubi⟧なのに、⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: Even though it was Sunday, my father went to work.

examples.japanese: ⟦{天気予報|てんきよほう}→天気予報：01678_tenkiyohou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{晴|は}れ→晴れ：02936_hare⟧だった。なのに、⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{降|ふ}っている→降る：00839_furu⟧。
examples.english: The forecast said it would be sunny. And yet it's been raining since morning.

entry.notes:
Formed from な (the copula/na-adjective connector) + ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (despite). Attaches to nouns and na-adjective stems. Very common in spoken Japanese, often expressing the speaker's frustration or complaint that reality did not match expectations.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- After nouns: ⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧なのに (despite being a student)
- After na-adjectives: ⟦{静|しず}か→静か：00755_shizuka⟧なのに (despite being quiet)
- Sentence-final use: ...なのに。(expressing frustration without completing the thought)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: despite — the broader particle; なのに is specifically the noun/na-adjective form
- けど / ⟦けれど→けれど：01990_keredo⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧: but — more neutral, less emotional than なのに
- ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧なのに: despite that — a longer, more emphatic version used at the start of a new sentence
- にもかかわらず: despite / in spite of — more formal written equivalent

REGISTER:
Casual to neutral. Very common in everyday spoken Japanese. The emotional nuance makes it less suitable for formal writing, where にもかかわらず is preferred.

USAGE:
When used at the end of a sentence (e.g., ⟦{日曜日|にちようび}→日曜日：00656_nichiyoubi⟧なのに...), the speaker leaves the complaint implied, creating a tone of disappointment or resignation.

definitions.gloss: same age group; same generation; peers
definitions.explanation: People who belong to the same age bracket or generation. Used to describe someone of roughly the same age, not necessarily the exact same year.

examples.japanese: {同年代|どうねんだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{同年代|どうねんだい}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: I think she's about the same age as me.

examples.japanese: {同年代|どうねんだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧たち⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{共通|きょうつう}→共通：02590_kyoutsuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{話題|わだい}→話題：03793_wadai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}つかり→見つかる：01173_mitsukaru⟧やすい。
examples.english: When I talk with people of the same generation, it's easy to find common topics.

entry.notes:
Composed of ⟦{同|どう}→同〜：03962_dou⟧ (same) and ⟦{年代|ねんだい}→年代：03533_nendai⟧ (age group/era). Refers to people who are roughly the same age — not necessarily born in the same year, but within the same general bracket (typically within about 5 years).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {同年代|どうねんだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: person of the same age group
- {同年代|どうねんだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧: children of the same age
- {同年代|どうねんだい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{比|くら}べて→比べる：01237_kuraberu⟧: compared with one's age group
- {同年代|どうねんだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{平均|へいきん}→平均：03614_heikin⟧: average for the age group

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{同世代|どうせだい}→同世代：17141_dousedai⟧: same generation — very close in meaning but emphasizes generational identity (shared cultural experiences) rather than just age
- {同年齢|どうねんれい}: same age — refers to the exact same age, more precise than {同年代|どうねんだい}
- ⟦{同期|どうき}→同期：12029_douki⟧: same year/cohort — people who entered a school or company in the same year

definitions.gloss: gliding; sliding; taxiing (of an aircraft)
definitions.explanation: The act of sliding or gliding along a surface. Most commonly used for aircraft taxiing on a runway, but also for skiing and skating.

examples.japanese: ⟦{飛行機|ひこうき}→飛行機：00629_hikouki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{滑走|かっそう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。
examples.english: The airplane began taxiing.

examples.japanese: ⟦{滑走路|かっそうろ}→滑走路：05980_kassouro⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}かって→向かう：01186_mukau⟧{滑走|かっそう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: To taxi toward the runway.

examples.japanese: ⟦スキー→スキー：03849_sukii⟧{場|じょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ゲレンデ→ゲレンデ：23907_gerende⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{気持|きも}ちよく→気持ちいい：09583_kimochiii⟧{滑走|かっそう}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I glided pleasantly down the ski slope.

entry.notes:
Composed of {滑|かっ} (slide/glide) and {走|そう} (run). The word covers any smooth sliding movement along a surface, but is most strongly associated with aircraft and skiing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{滑走路|かっそうろ}→滑走路：05980_kassouro⟧: runway
- {滑走|かっそう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to glide, to taxi
- {滑走|かっそう}⟦{距離|きょり}→距離：05331_kyori⟧: gliding/taxiing distance
- {滑走|かっそう}⟦{速度|そくど}→速度：03319_sokudo⟧: taxiing speed

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{滑|すべ}る→滑る：01230_suberu⟧: to slide/slip — the everyday verb for sliding; {滑走|かっそう} is more formal and implies sustained, purposeful movement
- ⟦{走行|そうこう}→走行：14260_soukou⟧: running/traveling — movement of vehicles on roads, not gliding
- ⟦{離陸|りりく}→離陸：05981_ririku⟧: takeoff — the act of leaving the ground, which follows {滑走|かっそう}

definitions.gloss: encirclement; siege; surrounding
definitions.explanation: The act of surrounding something or someone on all sides, whether in a military, police, or figurative context.

examples.japanese: ⟦{敵|てき}→敵：03546_teki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{包囲|ほうい}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。

examples.english: The castle was besieged from three sides, and food supplies were also cut off.

entry.notes:
Composed of {包|ほう} (wrap/enclose) and {囲|い} (surround). Describes the tactical or physical act of surrounding something. Common in military history, news reports about police operations, and figurative expressions about being cornered.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {包囲|ほうい}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to surround, to besiege
- {包囲|ほうい}{網|もう}: encirclement net, cordon
- {包囲|ほうい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{突破|とっぱ}する→突破する：25363_toppasuru⟧: to break through an encirclement
- {包囲|ほうい}⟦{攻撃|こうげき}→攻撃：02748_kougeki⟧: siege attack
- {包囲|ほうい}⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧: to be surrounded

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{囲|かこ}む→囲む：02037_kakomu⟧: to surround — the everyday verb for surrounding
- ⟦{取|と}り{囲|かこ}む→取り囲む：20925_torikakomu⟧: to surround / to encircle — emphasizes closing in from all sides

Composed of {焼|しょう} (burn) and {却|きゃく} (dispose of). A formal term for burning things to destroy them, most commonly associated with waste disposal. In Japan, incineration is a major method of waste management, and ⟦{焼却炉|しょうきゃくろ}→焼却炉：23880_shoukyakuro⟧ (incinerators) are found in many municipalities.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼却|しょうきゃく}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to incinerate
- ⟦{焼却炉|しょうきゃくろ}→焼却炉：23880_shoukyakuro⟧: incinerator
- {焼却|しょうきゃく}⟦{処分|しょぶん}→処分：05520_shobun⟧: disposal by incineration
- {焼却|しょうきゃく}⟦{施設|しせつ}→施設：02503_shisetsu⟧: incineration facility
- ⟦ごみ→ゴミ：00840_gomi⟧{焼却|しょうきゃく}{場|じょう}: waste incineration plant

SIMILAR WORDS:

- {消却|しょうきゃく}: write-off / amortization — a homophone with completely different meaning (financial)
- ⟦{廃棄|はいき}→廃棄：12482_haiki⟧: disposal / scrapping — broader term for disposing of things, not limited to burning

entry.gloss: how much; to what extent; how far

definitions.gloss: how much; to what extent; how far
definitions.explanation: An interrogative or exclamatory adverb asking about the degree or extent of something. Can also be used rhetorically to emphasize a great degree.

examples.english: How long do I have to wait?

examples.japanese: どれほど⟦{大変|たいへん}→大変：00594_taihen⟧だった⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦{想像|そうぞう}できる→想像する：06060_souzousuru⟧。
examples.english: I can imagine how hard it was.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧どれほど⟦{努力|どりょく}して→努力する：20201_doryokusuru⟧きた⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧、⟦{周|まわ}り→周り：01732_mawari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{知|し}っている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: The people around her know well how much effort she has put in.

entry.notes:
Composed of ⟦どれ→どれ：00547_dore⟧ (which/what) and ほど (degree/extent). Used both in genuine questions ('How much...?') and in rhetorical/emphatic statements to convey that something is to an impressive or significant degree. Slightly more literary than ⟦どの→どの：00551_dono⟧くらい.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- どれほど〜⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧: how much ~ (embedded question)
- どれほど〜て⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧: no matter how much ~
- どれほど〜こと⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧: how ~ it is! (exclamatory)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- どれほど⟦{嬉|うれ}しかった→嬉しい：00822_ureshii⟧こと⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧: how happy I was!
- どれほど⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{価値|かち}→価値：00131_kachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧: how much value it has
- どれほど⟦{時間|じかん}がかかる→時間がかかる：26082_jikangakakaru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧: how long it takes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦どの→どの：00551_dono⟧くらい: how much / how long — the most common everyday equivalent
- いかほど: how much — more formal and literary
- ⟦どれ→どれ：00547_dore⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧: how much — similar meaning, slightly more casual than どれほど

entry.gloss: to overdo it; to push oneself too hard; to strain oneself

definitions.gloss: to overdo it; to push oneself too hard; to strain oneself
definitions.explanation: To force oneself beyond reasonable limits, whether physically, mentally, or in terms of schedule and workload. Often used as advice or a warning.

examples.japanese: {無理|むり}しないで⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
examples.english: Don't push yourself too hard, okay?

examples.japanese: ⟦{体調|たいちょう}→体調：04644_taichou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧なら{無理|むり}しない⟦ほうがいい→ほうがいい：10078_hougaii⟧。
examples.english: If you're not feeling well, you shouldn't overdo it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{無理|むり}しすぎて、⟦{体|からだ}→体：00784_karada⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{壊|こわ}して→壊す：01241_kowasu⟧しまった。
examples.english: I pushed myself too hard at work and ruined my health.

entry.notes:
One of the most common everyday expressions in Japanese. Often heard as caring advice from friends, family, or coworkers. The phrase {無理|むり}しないで (don't overdo it) is a standard way to show concern for someone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無理|むり}しないで: don't push yourself
- {無理|むり}しすぎる: to overdo it too much
- ⟦{体|からだ}→体：00784_karada⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{無理|むり}する: to strain one's body
- {無理|むり}して⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧: to force oneself to work
- {無理|むり}して⟦{笑|わら}う→笑う：00685_warau⟧: to force a smile

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{頑張|がんば}る→頑張る：01222_ganbaru⟧: to do one's best — positive connotation of effort, while {無理|むり}する implies going beyond healthy limits
- ⟦{我慢|がまん}する→我慢する：25343_gamansuru⟧: to endure — focuses on tolerating discomfort, not necessarily pushing beyond limits

USAGE:
{無理|むり}する is often used in the negative to discourage someone from overdoing things. It carries a warm, caring tone. The noun ⟦{無理|むり}→無理：01558_muri⟧ alone means "unreasonable" or "impossible," but with ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ it shifts to mean pushing oneself beyond what is advisable.

entry.gloss: to prepare; to arrange; to have ready

definitions.gloss: to prepare; to arrange; to have ready
definitions.explanation: To make specific items or arrangements ready for use, often implying that the items will be needed soon or are being laid out for someone.

examples.japanese: ⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧ごはん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{用意|ようい}する。
examples.english: To prepare breakfast.

examples.japanese: お⟦{客|きゃく}→客：00865_kyaku⟧さま⟦{用|よう}→〜用：09842_you⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{椅子|いす}→椅子：00706_isu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{用意|ようい}→用意：01746_youi⟧⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I prepared chairs for the guests.

examples.japanese: ⟦{万|まん}が{一|いち}→万が一：17693_mangaichi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{備|そな}えて→備える：02125_sonaeru⟧、⟦{予備|よび}→予備：03993_yobi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦バッテリー→バッテリー：04425_batterii⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{用意|ようい}→用意：01746_youi⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧おいて⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please have a spare battery ready just in case.

entry.notes:
Focuses on having specific items or arrangements ready and at hand. More concrete and action-oriented than ⟦{準備|じゅんび}する→準備する：22427_junbisuru⟧, which covers broader preparation processes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{用意|ようい}する: to prepare a meal
- ⟦お{金|かね}→お金：00611_okane⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{用意|ようい}する: to have money ready
- ⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{用意|ようい}する: to prepare a seat
- ⟦{用意|ようい}→用意：01746_youi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧: it's ready
- ⟦{用意|ようい}→用意：01746_youi⟧ドン: ready, set, go!
- ⟦{用意|ようい}{周到|しゅうとう}→用意周到：19898_youishuutou⟧: thoroughly prepared

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{準備|じゅんび}する→準備する：22427_junbisuru⟧: to prepare — broader and more process-oriented; covers planning and organizing
- ⟦{支度|したく}する→支度する：01828_shitakusuru⟧: to get ready — personal preparation (getting dressed, packing)
- ⟦{整|ととの}える→整える：04259_totonoeru⟧: to arrange / to put in order — emphasizes organizing and tidying

USAGE:
The set phrase ⟦{用意|ようい}→用意：01746_youi⟧ドン is used to start races and games, equivalent to "ready, set, go!" The compound ⟦{用意|ようい}{周到|しゅうとう}→用意周到：19898_youishuutou⟧ (thorough preparation) is a common four-character idiom praising someone's careful planning.

entry.gloss: to sign; to put one's signature on

definitions.gloss: to sign; to put one's signature on
definitions.explanation: To write one's name on a document, petition, or other official paper to indicate agreement, authorization, or acknowledgment.

examples.japanese: ⟦{契約書|けいやくしょ}→契約書：06416_keiyakusho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{署名|しょめい}する。
examples.english: To sign a contract.

examples.japanese: ⟦ここ→ここ：00961_koko⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{署名|しょめい}→署名：03682_shomei⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please sign here.

examples.japanese: ⟦{両国|りょうこく}→両国：10010_ryoukoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{代表|だいひょう}→代表：03419_daihyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{条約|じょうやく}→条約：04912_jouyaku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{署名|しょめい}→署名：03682_shomei⟧し、⟦{歴史的|れきしてき}→歴史的：05671_rekishiteki⟧な⟦{合意|ごうい}→合意：05093_goui⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{成立|せいりつ}した→成立する：25497_seiritsusuru⟧。
examples.english: Representatives from both countries signed the treaty, and a historic agreement was reached.

entry.notes:
A formal word for signing documents. Used in legal, business, and diplomatic contexts. In everyday situations, ⟦サインする→サインする：09864_sainsuru⟧ is more commonly heard.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{署名|しょめい}→署名：03682_shomei⟧⟦{活動|かつどう}→活動：00201_katsudou⟧: signature campaign (petition drive)
- ⟦{署名|しょめい}→署名：03682_shomei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}める→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧: to collect signatures
- ⟦{署名|しょめい}→署名：03682_shomei⟧⟦{捺印|なついん}→捺印：08014_natsuin⟧: signature and seal
- ⟦{電子|でんし}→電子：03449_denshi⟧⟦{署名|しょめい}→署名：03682_shomei⟧: digital signature
- ⟦{署名|しょめい}{欄|らん}→署名欄：30137_shomeiran⟧: signature field

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦サインする→サインする：09864_sainsuru⟧: to sign — more casual and widely used in daily life (signing receipts, autographs)
- ⟦{記名|きめい}→記名：14862_kimei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to write one's name — simply writing one's name, without the legal weight of a signature
- ⟦{調印|ちょういん}→調印：14252_chouin⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to sign (a treaty) — specifically for signing international agreements or treaties

REGISTER:
Formal. Used in official and legal contexts. For casual situations like signing a credit card receipt, ⟦サインする→サインする：09864_sainsuru⟧ is more natural.
